## The near-miss

An agent preparing Gerrit change 2665 staged its commit message at the fixed path
`/tmp/commitmsg.txt`. A concurrent session working in `/Users/joeoakhart/windows-lock-s1` wrote to
**the same path**. The agent's `git commit -F /tmp/commitmsg.txt` then picked up the OTHER
session's message body — "Give the store write lock a Windows leg" — and attached it to its own,
completely unrelated diff (EBS mount assertions in `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`).

It was caught only because the agent read the commit back before pushing. It recovered with
`make amend-msg` (Change-Id preserved, so no duplicate change) and switched to a `mktemp -d` path.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Had it not read the commit back, a Gerrit change would have gone up for review carrying a **false
description of what it does**. Reviewers, the `rebar-ticket:` trailer audit, `git log`, and every
future bisect would all have agreed with each other and all been wrong. That is the same defect
class this session has spent the night filing — an artefact asserting something that was never
true — except lodged in the permanent commit record rather than in a check.

The conditions that produced it are not exotic. This host currently runs **eleven active
worktrees** across several concurrent agent sessions, all as the same OS user, all with `/tmp`
shared. A fixed filename under `/tmp` is not a race that might happen; it is a collision waiting
for two sessions to reach the same step, which on a busy night is minutes apart.

Note the asymmetry that makes it dangerous: the collision is SILENT. `git commit -F` succeeded,
exit 0, no warning. Nothing distinguishes "my message" from "someone else's message" at the point
of use — only a human or agent reading the result back can tell.

## Scope — this is about guidance and tooling, not one agent

The agent that hit it did the right things (read back, recovered without a duplicate change,
switched to `mktemp -d`, disclosed it prominently). The question is why a fixed `/tmp` path was
reachable at all:

- this session's own operating convention is a per-job scratch directory precisely for this
  reason, and that convention lives in the harness prompt rather than anywhere an agent working
  from repo guidance would find it;
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` document `make amend-msg` for message rewrites but say nothing
  about WHERE to stage a message body;
- nothing in the repo's tooling refuses or warns on a shared-`/tmp` path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Repo guidance states plainly that any scratch file — commit message bodies especially — must
      go in a per-session directory (`mktemp -d`, or the session's own scratch dir), never a fixed
      path under `/tmp`, because multiple agent sessions share this host as one OS user.
- [x] The reasoning is recorded with the guidance, not just the rule: the failure is SILENT and
      lands in the permanent commit record. A rule without its reason gets optimised away.
- [x] Consider whether `make amend-msg` and any commit-message helper should reject a path under
      `/tmp` that is not session-unique, or at minimum warn. Decide either way and record why —
      a guard is only worth adding if it cannot itself become noise.
- [x] Sweep the repo's scripts and documented workflows for other fixed `/tmp` paths that two
      concurrent sessions could collide on, and record each with a disposition. Enumerate the
      result; do not fix only the commit-message case.
